meta.description: Academic / vocational verification decision config per ANZSCO occupation. Decision logic and canonical subject lists only; naming variants live in the per-ANZSCO Consolidated Rubric.
meta.howToResolve: occupation = occupations[id]; flow = flows[occupation.flow]; any field absent on an occupation falls back to defaults. labels.* on an occupation override defaults.
knownIssues: Tier 2 bands in these occupations are written 7–8 / 5–5 / 3–3 / 0–1 (of 8), leaving scores 6, 4 and 2 undefined: materials-engineer, geotechnical-engineer, structural-engineer, transport-engineer, industrial-engineer, production-plant-engineer, petroleum-engineer, environmental-engineer, naval-architect. Encoded as minimum thresholds (7/5/3).
Determination matrices omit one combination in each flow (Flag + Medium; Medium + Not Met). Added as inferred rules, marked inferred=true.
Tier 3 appears in the docs as a gate but not in the determination matrix. Modelled as a post-step that downgrades auto-approve to manual review.
ANZSCO 233999 is used by two occupations (Automation & Control, Mechatronics). `id` is the unique key.
A single transcript subject may fill both a Tier 1 and a Tier 2 row in some occupations (e.g. Fluid Mechanics, Surveying). The docs do not say whether dual counting across tiers is allowed.

scoring.bandRule: Compare score to thresholds from highest to lowest; first threshold met wins. Below the last threshold: tier1 = flag, tier2/coreUnits = high.

matchingRules.namingVariantSource: Per-ANZSCO Consolidated Rubric (separate file). This config holds decision logic only.
